title: Change-diff eval fingerprinting & contextual notifications for canary rollouts
creator: Marisol Chen
description:
Problem: When model or config changes are pushed we run evals and may receive noisy, duplicate regression notifications in Console (Slack/PagerDuty). During canary or staged rollouts this generates false-positive incidents and creates alert fatigue for SREs and product owners.

Goal: Implement a change-diff driven pipeline that computes a compact fingerprint for a code/config/model delta, runs targeted evals, and surfaces contextualized notifications in the Console. Fingerprinting and heuristics should enable deduplication across correlated regressions, reduce PD noise during canary windows, and attach provenance (PR/commit/config ID) to every notification so owners can act quickly.

Scope: Console UI surfaces (change-diff view, fingerprint score, suggested suppression duration), notification routing (Slack channel routing, PagerDuty incident gating), alert dedupe logic (fingerprint similarity thresholding), and eval orchestration hooks (targeted eval runs on detected diffs). Backend work includes telemetry changes, new eval metadata fields, and a deploy-time signal for staged rollout windows.
acceptance_criteria: When a model/config change is pushed, Console shows a Change-Diff card linking to the eval run and PR/commit metadata
Notifications include a 'Fingerprint ID' and similarity score; Console groups notifications with fingerprint similarity >= configurable threshold
Canary/staged rollouts can auto-suppress PD incidents for first N hours and instead route condensed notices to a single Slack channel thread
Operators can override suppression from the Console (promote to PD) and suppression decisions are logged for audit
Aggregated regression telemetry (per-fingerprint) available in the Evals dashboard with time series for metric deltas and affected prompt sets
End-to-end tests validate dedupe behavior across three simulated deployments where same regression shows on 3, 5, and 80% rollout windows
Telemetry emitted: change_id, fingerprint_id, fingerprint_score, eval_run_id, routed_destinations, suppression_reason
No increase in 95th percentile eval latency beyond 5% due to fingerprint computation
notes: Design trade-offs considered: compute fingerprints deterministically at CI vs post-deploy. Chosen approach: compute lightweight fingerprint at CI (PR stage) and finalize after model artifact build to ensure stable provenance.

Fingerprint algorithm: Jaccard-style similarity over normalized config diffs + signature of changed model files + weighted eval-set impact vectors. Exact algorithm to be reviewed by ENG and Research teams.
Fallback policy: if fingerprinting service is unavailable, revert to existing regression alerts (no suppression) to avoid missing critical incidents.
Rollout suppression policy: default 6-hour canary suppression window configurable per project with escalation if regression persists beyond window or affects >X% of traffic.
Privacy: provenance metadata will exclude PII and sensitive customer identifiers; only deploy metadata and PR/commit authors are stored.
Open question: Should fingerprint similarity be learned (ML) or rule-based thresholds? Start with rule-based and collect labeled matches for future ML model.
Consideration: Tagging alerts with model-variant and quantization-profile to avoid mixing regressions caused by quantization vs model weights changes.
implementation_plan: 1) Instrument CI to emit change_id and preliminary fingerprint when a PR builds (ENG-20577 dependency)
2) Add eval-run metadata fields: change_id, fingerprint_id, fingerprint_score, provenance refs
3) Implement fingerprint similarity service and dedupe API used by Console and Alert Router
4) Console UI: Change-Diff card, grouped notification stream, and suppression controls
5) Notification layer: route to Slack thread for suppressed canaries and gate PD incidents until suppression conditions expire
6) End-to-end QA: simulated rollouts with staged percentages using a local harness and canary windows
7) Monitor: create dashboard panels for fingerprint hit-rate, suppressed-to-promoted incidents, and false-suppression rate
8) Gradual rollout behind feature flag per org; start with internal buckets, then beta customers
risks: Over-suppression could hide real regressions — mitigated by easy promote-to-PD action and short default suppression windows
Fingerprint collisions may cause unrelated regressions to be grouped — will introduce adjustable similarity thresholds and manual unlinking
Increased data storage and telemetry costs for provenance and fingerprint time series — accounted for in release planning
Operational complexity for customers with multiple concurrent rollouts; will provide per-org configuration and documentation
qa_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint generation and similarity scoring
Integration tests covering eval-run metadata propagation from CI -> eval service -> Console
E2E tests using synthetic diffs to validate dedupe behavior across Slack + PagerDuty
Load test fingerprint service at expected peak eval-run rates to ensure <100ms p99 compute time
deployment_plan: Feature gated rollout: internal -> beta orgs -> GA
Migration: backfill fingerprint_id for recent 7 days of eval runs for historical grouping
Alerting: monitor suppressed-to-promoted ratio and customer support tickets related to missed regressions
Rollback: if suppression causes operational issues, flip feature flag to disable suppression only (keep grouping for visibility)
updates: 2026-03-02: Scoping workshop completed with ENG and Research. Agreed to start with rule-based similarity thresholds.
2026-03-05: Prototype fingerprint PoC shows 92% grouping accuracy on historical eval dataset (internal).
2026-03-09: UX mocks reviewed; PM and Design approved primary card; minor copy edits requested for suppression affordance.
2026-03-12: ENG merged telemetry schema PR; backend fields ready for eval-run ingestion.
2026-03-14: Started work on Console grouping API; Diego to coordinate with SRE on PagerDuty gating rules.
final_notes: Priority is to reduce alert fatigue during staged rollouts while preserving fast escalation for widespread regressions. Next step: onboarding beta orgs and collecting labeled grouping examples to iterate on similarity thresholds.
